actions.reason:
In _GPT4_SPLIT_PATTERN_STD (the standard library re form of the GPT-4 split pattern used by encode), the letter-run alternative "(?:[^
\w]|_)?[^\W\d_]+" is rewritten as "[^
\w]?[^\W\d_]+|_[^\W\d_]+". The two forms match the same text in the same order of attempts. '_' is a word character, so it never matches [^
\w] and is handled by the second branch, in the same place the original tried it. The rewrite removes an optional group with a branch inside, which sre runs through its general REPEAT/MAX_UNTIL machinery. That alternative is tried at almost every chunk start. The new form is a single-character optional class, which sre handles with its fast single-character repeat. The patch changes 2 lines in minbpe/regex.py. Outputs are identical on the equivalence harness. encode_ir ratio is 0.9835; the other metrics are unchanged within ±0.05%.

diff --git a/minbpe/regex.py b/minbpe/regex.py
--- a/minbpe/regex.py
+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -28,7 +28,7 @@ GPT2_SPLIT_PATTERN = r"""'(?:[sdmt]|ll|ve|re)| ?\p{L}+| ?\p{N}+| ?[^\s\p{L}\p{N}
 GPT4_SPLIT_PATTERN = r"""'(?i:[sdmt]|ll|ve|re)|[^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?+\p{L}+|\p{N}{1,3}| ?[^\s\p{L}\p{N}]++[\r\n]*|\s*[\r\n]|\s+(?!\S)|\s+"""
 # GPT4_SPLIT_PATTERN for the standard library re module, valid when letters are
 # [^\W\d_], numbers are \d and whitespace is \s in both modules
-_GPT4_SPLIT_PATTERN_STD = r"""'(?i:[sdmt]|ll|ve|re)|(?:[^\r\n\w]|_)?[^\W\d_]+|\d{1,3}| ?(?:[^\s\w]|_)+[\r\n]*|\s*[\r\n]|\s+(?!\S)|\s+"""
+_GPT4_SPLIT_PATTERN_STD = r"""'(?i:[sdmt]|ll|ve|re)|[^\r\n\w]?[^\W\d_]+|_[^\W\d_]+|\d{1,3}| ?(?:[^\s\w]|_)+[\r\n]*|\s*[\r\n]|\s+(?!\S)|\s+"""
 
 
 class RegexTokenizer(Tokenizer):

journal.text:
I worked on encode_ir in minbpe/regex.py. The first two attempts edited the code around lines 493-516 and the imports at lines 12-14. The final change touched only _GPT4_SPLIT_PATTERN_STD. It rewrites the letter-run alternative "(?:[^\r\n\w]|_)?[^\W\d_]+" as "[^\r\n\w]?[^\W\d_]+|_[^\W\d_]+".

Evaluation 1 was rejected with encode_ir ratio 1.0361. Evaluation 3 was rejected with ratio 1.0160. Both made encode slower, so I dropped them. Evaluation 5 was accepted. encode_ir went from 541520764 to 532578512, ratio 0.9835. The other metrics stayed between 0.9999 and 1.0005, and outputs were identical. It is submitted as a 2-line change, queued for replay.

Restructuring the code around the pattern cost more than it saved. The pattern itself was the cheaper lever. '_' is a word character, so it never matches [^\r\n\w]. The split keeps the same match order.

Next I will look at the other alternatives in _GPT4_SPLIT_PATTERN_STD for optional groups that can be split the same way.
